answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a marble, before it can post or attest. A single bridge checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 339 aliases as a result costs 448 bonds held for 9 days each, plus the cipher attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
